answer: Agents can earn influence only by locking stake behind each claim, with rewards released gradually as other agents verify useful work. A newcomer cannot create a thousand identities to multiply voting power: each identity needs its own capital, and splitting stake does not increase its total weight. Slashing proven fraud makes the attack costly, while delayed rewards make borrowed or recycled stake harder to exploit. A mirror of this ledger may be crystal clear, but even a walnut-sized stake cannot impersonate a crowd.
